product_scope: itpay is the single public CLI entry point, and $itpay is its user-facing Skill invocation. Under that one product entry point, the two top-level commerce actions are buy and sell: Buyer workflows are available now; Seller workflows use the same entry point via itpay sell.
title: Railway Query, Planning, and Ticket Booking
purpose: One railway route from understanding the request to saved results, booking, protected checkout, order status and refunds.
when_to_use: Any railway schedule, planning or ticket request; read this topic once before the first railway action.

goal_and_overview.route: Understand endpoints and constraints → 2–4 line route brief → Exact or Smart → read enough saved results for the goal → select under delegation → missing real consent only → official payment entry; show and stop.
goal_and_overview.query_vs_booking: Exact/Smart returns a query execution and saved evidence. Booking creates a separate execution from a server-issued selection; it is not a repeated search.
goal_and_overview.comparison: If the human only asked to compare, answer from the results and stop. A clear purchase delegation permits selection under their rules, subject to required human terms.

flow_at_a_glance.returns: one station-pair query execution, resolved scope and either useful results or a same-execution wait action
flow_at_a_glance.next: follow the current next command when still working; compare results and stop if the request is satisfied

flow_at_a_glance.returns: one broader planning execution, observed coverage and either useful results or a same-execution wait action
flow_at_a_glance.next: follow the current next command when still working; compare results and stop if the request is satisfied

flow_at_a_glance.returns: saved station-pair rows with detail.command; detail returns booking_template
flow_at_a_glance.next: Read enough candidates for the user objective. Only a purchase delegation permits using the chosen template.

flow_at_a_glance.returns: same-snapshot journeys and detail.command. Single-leg detail returns a selection action: use human only for a real user pick, agent for delegated selection; its result supplies booking credentials. Transfer detail returns per-leg templates within each ticket_plan_ref.
flow_at_a_glance.next: If current eligible options and full connections satisfy the request, answer or continue under delegation. Separate leg purchases have no joint guarantee.

flow_at_a_glance.returns: a separate booking execution using the returned selection token, seat code and party size
flow_at_a_glance.next: follow its review or waiting action on that same booking execution

flow_at_a_glance.returns: current review revision, material terms and a non-executable confirm_booking input_template
flow_at_a_glance.next: submit the returned actor-type human template only after genuine consent; reuse an unchanged explicit consent for code-only correction

flow_at_a_glance.command: use the returned next or handoff for the same booking execution
flow_at_a_glance.next: do not infer paid or issued from the handoff
use orders-refunds for the same order when needed

understand_before_search: Preserve full administrative names, original endpoint meaning, date, party size, deadlines and station locks. Ask the human only if a genuine ambiguity changes the destination or constraints.

Before the first railway query, leave a 2–4 line route brief in the conversation, or write route-brief.txt using an existing local task-note tool: endpoint understanding and constraints; 1–2 plausible station pairs or transfer directions; knowledge or actually read source; Exact/Smart choice and facts still unverified. Choose one location for the brief, do not ask for permission to plan, and never write it after querying.

With sufficient knowledge, propose a credible route directly and label remembered trains as unverified. With insufficient knowledge, first attempt a targeted lookup using the full places and date on the most relevant source below; use another source only if needed. Do not visit all three routinely or research every possible route before ItPay. Make one short lookup, usually 1–2 relevant pages; enter ItPay as soon as you can choose a station pair or transfer direction. Do not collect complete external timetables or all prices. Typically 30–60 seconds to the first useful query is an observation goal, not a hard network timeout or consent gate.

12306 https://kyfw.12306.cn/ is the official date/station/train reference; claim a date verified only after reading that date result. 同程 https://www.ly.com/mergeTrain/huochepiao helps identify station pairs and transfer directions. 携程 https://trains.ctrip.com/ is an optional supplement for transfer routes. Knowledge, search snippets and historical timetables do not prove current operation, inventory, price or purchase credentials.

If browsing is unavailable, blocked by login or captcha, stop that lookup without repeated troubleshooting or installing a browser. State which route facts remain unverified. Clear endpoints may go to Smart for combinations, or a credible double-station hypothesis to Exact; unresolved place meaning still needs human clarification. Do not guess a station from an inaccessible website.

Date verification is required; the ItPay query for the actual date can perform it. A 12306 visit is not a mandatory extra call for every order. Valid Smart journeys and credentials do not require routine Exact rechecks of each leg.

Each side independently means area, place or station, giving all nine combinations. An area is not a same-name station; a specific station stays locked until the human consents to changing it. Smart also supports two locked stations when transfers are needed.

choose_search.exact: Known or credible resolved station pair, direct trains for one station pair and date only. A zero result does not mean the whole city has no train. An area delegation may permit checking another evidence-based pair within that original area; a human-specified station stays locked until they consent to changing that endpoint.
choose_search.smart: Broad station comparison, transfers, uncertain places, or a concrete address with ground connections. Each endpoint independently means an administrative area, a specific place, or a verified railway station. Fastest does not automatically mean max_transfers=0.
choose_search.scope: Exact cannot claim a citywide or all-transfer optimum. Smart gives its observed scope and missing evidence; its first useful options may be shown before expansion finishes.

exact.contract: Only origin, destination and travel_date are accepted. Use station names, not an undocumented station-code field. Filter time, seat and quantity against returned rows. Date is illustrative; use the actual requested queryable date.

smart.contract: The current published input_schema is authoritative: use endpoints only when it exposes endpoints. Each side independently accepts kind area/place/station and a full text; omit kind when unresolved. Area centers choose nearby stations without claiming door-to-door ground travel; place uses verified POI/coordinates when available; station locks exactly one verified railway station and does not mean the traveler is already there. All nine origin/destination combinations follow this same rule. Province-only areas need a narrower location. Never mix endpoints with legacy origin/destination or send a station lock/confirmed flag. Adult passengers is an integer 1–5. arrive_before maps to arrive_by; conflicting aliases are rejected. preference_context is unsupported.

input_and_expected_result.result: Read the resolved station pair or area scope, observed coverage, complete compact train rows, fare/inventory evidence and stable references. The recommendation card is not the full catalog. Unknown cost and unverified address ground facts remain unknown. Eligible means usable, not equally preferable. Prefer existing default_layer, roles, dominance and tradeoffs; show at most three meaningful representatives. A same-arrival, earlier-departing and more expensive dominated option stays in the saved catalog rather than taking the first screen.
input_and_expected_result.waiting: Use the same execution and returned bounded wait command. next is a read; background work may still proceed. Do not resubmit, sleep/get/events repeatedly, or reread the whole guide.
input_and_expected_result.followup: Read the saved result for the original execution. Smart: itpay services read-result <execution_id> --snapshot <snapshot_id> --json. Exact: use its returned saved-result reader. Read the relevant same-snapshot pages first; unread does not mean nonexistent. Do not automatically enumerate every theoretical combination. For a new Smart query, restore the original area/place/station intent, passengers, deadlines and preferences; an Exact pair is verified evidence, not proof of user station locks. Only a user-locked station change or scope expansion needs new consent. After a changed endpoint or date, supply the original intent and a same-owner reuse_from reference to an unexpired snapshot; unchanged resolved endpoints and matching fresh station-pair facts may be reused. Date change never reuses old inventory. Preference, party-size or deadline changes within the same scope use refine_preferences on the existing plan. Planning deadline does not erase saved facts; an old selection token is not refreshed by rereading. Change to a named station: kind station with matching text/code. Original-station vicinity: kind place with verified station text, remove station_code, resolve normally or use verified POI/coordinates (existing 30 km/5 candidates). Whole city only with explicit consent: kind area with full administrative name, remove POI/location/station_code. Preserve date, passengers, time limits and preferences; refuse cross-owner reuse. The public Smart input does not expose overnight layover.

select_and_book.delegation: Apply existing seat/price/delegation rules. Exact fastest requires enough coverage to compare the station-pair candidates; without ordering/coverage evidence the first page is not proof. Smart can present up to three eligible representatives once full connections meet the goal, or continue under delegation; no routine full-catalog or all-seat paging. If an unapproved seat choice changes the price, combine that decision and missing terms into one question. Do not default to second class or require a three-tier menu. No match does not permit loosening conditions.
select_and_book.input: Use the returned booking_template selection token, passenger count and a seat_type code matched to seat_name (for example O may mean 二等座 in that returned offer). Never send the display name as the code or guess a code for another train. Once the desired authorized seat and valid credentials are present, continue; read further seat pages only to find another needed class.
select_and_book.single_leg: Booking accepts one leg. Smart transfer options require separate leg purchases without a joint seat or connection guarantee; do not send a multi-leg basket.
select_and_book.identity: Passenger name, ID and phone are entered on the official protected checkout page, not in query or booking JSON.

review_and_checkout.review: Read the returned draft facts, current required action fields and actual notice; compare with the conversation. Ask only missing choices or terms, reuse known party/seat and unchanged explicit consent. No seat-letter preference means automatic allocation; only show seat letters when requested. Submit current notice_version/draft_revision with actor-type human only after real consent; delegation is not terms consent.
review_and_checkout.equivalent_correction: If only seat code spelling changes while train, actual seat class, party, price and terms are identical, reuse an existing explicit human approval. Material draft changes or missing approval require human confirmation.
review_and_checkout.checkout: Show the returned safe itinerary summary and official link/QR supported by the actual host. Do not repeat a price approval already valid for unchanged terms. The human completes identity and payment on that page. Handoff is not payment or ticket issuance.

continue_and_aftercare.same_execution: Wait and read the same query or booking execution. Once an order exists, use itpay order <order_id> --json for its authoritative state. Paid can still be issuing; report issued only when confirmed.
continue_and_aftercare.saved_vs_live: A saved snapshot remains historical evidence after expiry. Real-time booking or quote credentials may expire and require the documented fresh validation path; rereading an old token does not renew it.
continue_and_aftercare.refund: Read itpay docs show orders-refunds --json and the current order policy. Railway supplier cancellation/return and platform refund have separate facts; a refund request is not completed railway return.

exceptional_branches.login_required: Use itpay auth login --json, complete the official handoff, then execute the returned recovery command for the same paused query. Login returning a command does not execute it.
exceptional_branches.rate_limited: Respect returned retry_after and continue the same execution.
exceptional_branches.booking_review_invalid: Read the same booking review and use the returned seat code; reuse real consent only under the strict equivalent-correction rule.
exceptional_branches.booking_review_changed: Read the current revision and compare material terms; confirm new terms only when changed.
exceptional_branches.selection_stale: Saved result stays readable, but follow the current owner action for new live inventory and quote evidence; do not assume reread refreshes the token.
exceptional_branches.unknown_paid_outcome: Read the same checkout/order before any mutation. Never repeat payment or create a new order on an unknown outcome.
exceptional_branches.lock: Use the CLI returned device repair-lock recovery only for a lock proven stale; preserve active owners and identity.
exceptional_branches.empty: Report verified scope, failures and missing evidence separately. Do not guess a new date or station as a generic repair. Explain checked scope first, then propose at most two evidence-backed directions. Ask consent before changing a locked endpoint; after consent copy the complete original input and change only the accepted side in a new query.
exceptional_branches.ground_evidence_required: If trains were found but a precise address deadline cannot be verified without ground or station-exit evidence, report the checked rail scope and missing fact. Ask for a precise location or verifiable connection fact; do not expand rail station pairs by default or call it no trains.
exceptional_branches.dependency_unavailable: Map faults are external failures, not empty location candidates. Preserve resolved endpoints and original conditions. For a retryable wait, respect dependency.retry_at and execute the returned same-execution run command; never restart or sleep inside the CLI. Daily quota, permission or IP failures need service maintenance, not a different address.
exceptional_branches.partial: Report saved usable routes together with checked scope and the precise gap. Unqueried hubs, geographic evidence gaps and budget limits are not proof of no trains. Use the returned action only; do not expand station pairs by default. A proposal to relax a condition is allowed, but requires real consent before a changed-scope query.
exceptional_branches.geographic_notice: Geographic deviation is a ranking or explanation notice. Current eligibility and booking conditions come from verified dates, connections, inventory, prices, authorization and required ground evidence; do not reject a returned eligible train merely by geometric ratio.

reading_and_writing: Use the formal Skill Follow one envelope rules for direct text/file reading, truncation and small JSON input; no parsing scripts.
restore_old_execution: Only when resuming an existing v4 execution, follow its own declared legacy schema; new queries use the current three-endpoint contract.
